title: privileged-access-chaos-testing-and-evidence-validation-guide-2026
author: Sofia Ramirez
body:
Overview

Purpose: This document defines a repeatable, low-risk program for chaos-testing privileged access controls across Redwood Inference services and validating that the resultant telemetry and compliance evidence meet audit and legal requirements. The activity intentionally exercises failure modes for RBAC, audit logging, credential rotation, and evidence packaging so we can proactively find gaps in detection, retention, and forensics.

Scope
- Systems: authz-service (policy engine), identity-proxy, privileged-session-proxy, audit-pipeline (event-enricher -> s3-archive -> indexer), kms-key-service, and model-serving control plane.
- Domains: RBAC enforcement, session elevation/just-in-time workflows, audit event delivery, log retention/archival, SDLC gating for privileged changes, and incident escalation.
- Excluded: customer-managed private deployments unless explicitly onboarded for a test run.

Goals
1. Verify that every privileged-action yields: authorization decision event, session context, user identity provenance, and immutable audit record in the archive within the delivery SLO.
2. Ensure evidence bundles are complete for at least 3 representative incident scenarios (credential compromise, mis-scoped role, replayed session token).
3. Measure detection latency for anomalous privileged activity and validate alerting/investigation playbooks produce required artifacts.

Success Criteria (must be met to mark run as green)
- Audit event delivery to cold-archive within 5 minutes for 95% of events and within 30 minutes for 99.9%.
- All evidence bundles for test scenarios include: decision-log, session-record, correlated network flow, kms key-use record, and commit/signoff metadata.
- No customer data is exposed during the test (see Data Residency & Safety checklist).

Prerequisites
1. Test window approved by security leadership and affected service owners.
2. Planned maintenance page and runbook published to oncall and SRE (link to related_pages).
3. Canary environment mirrors production authz policies and pipeline; backups of policy-store are taken.
4. Safety toggles in identity-proxy to auto-revoke test sessions on unexpected propagation.
5. Evidence collection container image built: registry.redwood.internal/priv-chaos-evidence:v1.

Test matrix (summary table)
(Note: this is a plain-text table; expand during run planning)
Scenario | Target Service | RBAC Vector | Expected Artifacts | Severity (test)
1) JIT elevation failure | identity-proxy -> authz-service | privilege escalation via allowed-flow | decision.log, session.dump, audit.event, kms.access | medium
2) Stale entitlement replay | privileged-session-proxy | replayed token after deprovision | authorization.denied, anomaly.alert, archival.event | high
3) Mis-scoped role change | policy-store -> model-serving | role grants unintended write | decision.log, git.commit.signoff, rollback.trace | high
4) Audit pipeline backlog | audit-pipeline indexer | delayed delivery due to partition | delivery.alert, archive.index_mismatch | medium

Execution procedure (step-by-step)
1. Pre-test validation (T-48h): Confirm policy-store snapshot, run synthetic tracer to validate audit pipeline throughput (example CLI):
   $ python tools/audit_tracer.py --env canary --rate 50 --duration 300
   Expected: 0 dropped events, 99% delivered to indexer within 120s.
2. Safety checklist (T-2h): Notify customer success for enterprise customers in affected regions; set maintenance mode on console routes that perform real billing-affecting actions.
3. Execute Scenario 1 (JIT elevation failure):
   a. Inject a synthetic JIT request via test harness targeting identity-proxy with a feature-flagged path: /v1/test/jit-elevate.
   b. Observe authz-service decision (query decision API):
      $ curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TEST_TOKEN}" https://authz-service.internal/decision?id=test-jit | jq
   c. Capture session dump using session-recorder: session-recorder --id ${SESSION_ID} --out /tmp/evidence/session1.json
   d. Verify audit-pipeline contains correlated event: indexer-query "event_type:authorization AND session_id:${SESSION_ID}"
4. Execute Scenario 2 and 3 similarly with scaled load and role-change operations executed as a scheduled, automated job.
5. Pipeline backlog simulation (Scenario 4): Pause indexer for 10 minutes (maintenance API) and replay 10k synthetic events; verify delivery SLA and alerting.

Evidence collection checklist (must be attached to post-test report)
- decision.log slices (authz-service) for each test transaction (ISO8601 timestamps)
- session dump (session-recorder output) containing: principal id, role bindings, origin IP, device fingerprint
- archive index snapshot and object keys (s3://audit-archive/2026-02-XX/*)
- kms key-use audit entries (kms-key-service events)
- commit/signoff metadata from policy-store (git sha + CI build link)
- alert context and investigation notes if detection fired

Verification queries and quick checks
- Count of authZ decisions per session:
  SELECT count(*) FROM audit_index WHERE session_id = "${SESSION_ID}" AND event_type = "authorization_decision";
- Correlate KMS usage to decision: filter audit_index where resource = "kms/key/redwood-priv-1" AND session_id = "${SESSION_ID}"
- Verify immutability: compare archive object checksum to index record checksum (sha256).

Data residency & safety rules (must be enforced for every test)
- No production PII or customer payloads may be used in synthetic tests. If production identifiers are required for provenance checks, use mapped pseudonymous identifiers and record mapping in a separate, encrypted evidence store.
- All archive copies created for test evidence must be tagged "test:evidence:true" and auto-pruned after 30 days unless retention approval is granted.

SDLC & change control gating
- Any policy changes required for a test must follow standard SDLC gates: feature branch -> CI security checks -> canary -> signed approval by policy-owner -> deploy.
- Tests that involve modifying policy-store require two approvers and must be performed during a scheduled deployment window.

Rollout, monitoring, and rollback
- Rollout approach: canary in canary environment -> limited org test (internal teams) -> broader run.
- Monitoring: dashboards to watch: authz-decision-latency, audit-pipeline-drop-rate, kms-usage-per-minute, session-revoke-rate. Alert thresholds:
  - authz-decision-latency > 300 ms (P1)
  - archive missing events > 0.1% over 15 min (P1)
- Rollback: any P1 alert during execution triggers immediate halt and automatic rollback of policy changes and session revocations. Use the policy-store rollback CLI:
  $ policy-store rollback --to-sha <snapshot-sha> --reason "chaos-test rollback"

Post-test analysis and evidence packaging
1. Assemble an evidence bundle per scenario into a signed tarball:
   $ tools/pack_evidence --inputs decision.log session.dump kms.events index.snapshot --out bundle-scenario1.tar.gz --signer security-team-key
2. Validate bundle contents against checklist and publish metadata to evidence-catalog (internal service) with fields: scenario_id, start_ts, end_ts, owners, S3 keys (comma separated).
3. Run automated verification: evidence-validator --bundle bundle-scenario1.tar.gz --schema privileged-evidence-v1.json
4. Publish a post-test report including: timeline, detection times, missing artifacts, mitigation actions, and recommended remediation tickets (link to backlog).

Escalation and incident-response integration
- If an unintentional customer impact occurs immediately: follow the incident-response-security playbook, page Incident Commander, and preserve unaltered copies of evidence for legal hold.
- For discovered gaps in evidence completeness: create a P0 remediation ticket with defined SLO to close within 14 days.

Risk and mitigations
- Risk: Test accidentally triggers live privileged operations. Mitigation: run in canary, use safety toggles, maintenance-mode for dangerous routes.
- Risk: Evidence leakage to non-authorized teams. Mitigation: encrypted evidence store, RBAC on evidence-catalog, test tags and auto-prune.

Ownership and cadence
- Run owner: Security Engineering (primary) — contact: security-eng@redwood.ai
- Service owner(s): listed in related_pages and must be present during run.
- Cadence: Quarterly by default; immediate re-run required after any production-sensitive RBAC incident.

Appendix A — Example audit event (text sample)
{
  "timestamp": "2026-02-15T15:04:05Z",
  "event_type": "authorization_decision",
  "principal": "user:svc-ci-deployer",
  "session_id": "sess-9a7b2c",
  "decision": "DENY",
  "policy_sha": "abc123def456",
  "resource": "model-serving:deploy:team-a",
  "reason": "role_missing:deploy_write",
  "correlation_id": "corr-xyz-001"
}

Appendix B — Remediation ticket template (use in post-test)
- Summary: [short description]
- Impact: [e.g., gaps in audit delivery, missing kms entries]
- Steps to reproduce: [link to scenario harness and timestamps]
- Owner: [team]
- Target SLA: 14 days

- audit-pipeline runbook: /confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/event-schema-contract-and-retention-runbook-2025

Notes: This guide is intended to be operational and will be updated after each run with lessons learned and concrete remediation PRs.
